desk.headline: Revenue up 15% to $772.4m and adjusted EPS of $0.73, both above estimates; FY27 revenue outlook kept below consensus; CEO to step down
results: Revenue grew 15% to $772.4m, above the $762m estimate; adjusted EPS of $0.73 beat the $0.61 estimate.
Annual recurring revenue rose 15% to $2.63bn; the company said it beat all of its own guided figures.
Non-GAAP operating margin jumped to a record 32.1% from 19.7% as non-GAAP costs fell 5%.
Free cash flow was $209.3m, up from $174.5m; Nutanix spent about $50m on buybacks.
Separately, the board has started a search for a new CEO; Rajiv Ramaswami stays until a successor takes over.

guidance.summary: Nutanix kept its FY27 revenue range of $3.18–3.23bn, slightly below consensus, but lifted its margin target by half a point and free cash flow by $25m, according to call coverage. Q2 revenue guidance of $820–830m is in line.

points: Management called demand healthy, but Q1 bookings dipped slightly as sales accounts were reshuffled and fewer large deals closed.
Server lead times have settled, but memory and chip shortages keep hardware prices high, which can slow some deals.
Support for outside storage systems, such as Dell and NetApp, was flagged as possibly the biggest growth driver over the next year.
Many prospects are customers leaving VMware after Broadcom's changes; it is too early to judge VMware's new lower-priced offer.
Q3 revenue is expected to fall by a mid-to-high single-digit percentage from Q2, a steeper seasonal dip than in recent years.
